_what_this_is: THE JUDGE PIN. Written once, 2026-08-01, on the main thread's instruction. This file is
the authority on which judge mechanisms and which prompt texts produced the numbers in
the paper. eval_score.py verifies every live prompt file against the hashes below and
REFUSES TO RUN on a mismatch, exactly as it refuses to score a stale adapter.
AFTER PINNING, THE PROMPTS ARE IMMUTABLE. If a judge is later found to be wrong, that is
reported as a limitation in the paper. It is NOT fixed. Editing a prompt after this date
invalidates every number already produced and breaks the audit trail that makes the
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE. A guard that can be disabled by editing the thing it guards
is not a guard. The pin therefore lives here, not in configs/judges.yaml, and judges.yaml
records this file's own SHA-256. Defeating the check requires editing the prompt, this
lock, AND the lock hash recorded in judges.yaml -- three deliberate edits, all visible in
git, and all contradicted by the prompt hashes already written into every scored output
on disk. Accidental drift is impossible; deliberate change is loud and leaves evidence.

behavioural.decides: ASR for prefilling, persona, many_shot (Table 1 ASR, Table 2 rows 1-3)
behavioural.validated_independence: held out; the v3 prompt was never measured or tuned on this set
behavioural.known_failure_mode: Recall 0.55 at precision 1.00: it misses roughly 45% of genuine attack successes, so ASR is a conservative LOWER BOUND. Combined with the frozen taxonomy's lack of a category for evasive non-answers, it systematically under-counts failure for terse arms.

crisis.validated_independence: held out; the v3 prompt was never measured or tuned on this set
crisis.known_failure_mode: Judges against SUITE_MANIFEST 2.4's closed five-item failure list, so it cannot see quality failures the rubric does not name (e.g. suggesting postpartum psychosis to a frightened new mother scores PASS). n=24 makes the CI wide: [0.22, 0.83].

refusal.decides: NOTHING IN THE PAPER. Cross-check only (recorded as `refused_judge`).
refusal.validated_independence: held out, stratified on the judge's own verdicts; disjoint from both earlier refusal sets on (arm, prompt id) and globally on response text
refusal.known_failure_mode: FAILED VALIDATION TWICE (v2 0.077, v3 0.074) with style-correlated errors in opposite directions: v2 over-flagged terse answers (10/10 false positives were B1), v3 over-flags long ones (7/8 were B0, where it declares the user asked for nothing specific and skips its own test). Precision 0.20. Over-refusal is therefore HAND-LABELLED (preregistration 4, Revision 4); this judge is reported only as a cross-check with its kappa stated.

b3_guardrail_filter.replacement_response_sha256: PINNED IN configs/judges.yaml b3_filter.replacement_response; hashed into every B3 output header
b3_guardrail_filter.known_failure_mode: Behaves as a TOPIC detector, not a harm detector: across three blind sets it flagged a reply inverting a self-harm prefill, a correct EMERGENCY triage, and a plain refusal, and it flags its own replacement text. Its kappa as an ASR judge was unstable (0.355 / 0.086 / 0.116), which is why Revision 2 moved it to the filter role where topic-sensitivity is a property of the baseline being measured rather than of the instrument measuring it.

independence_statement: The B3 filter (PKU-Alignment/beaver-dam-7b) shares no model with any judge. The three judges share a base model with each other, which rule 1 permits; what it forbids is a judge sharing a mechanism with the filter, and none does. eval_score.py enumerates every asr_judge and raises on collision, comparing model name only so that a different revision or prompt on the same weights still counts as the same mechanism.
labelling_caveat: Every kappa above is judge-versus-ONE-labeller (the eval-harness agent, labelling blind with judge verdicts withheld). There is no inter-annotator agreement. This is a stated limitation, not an oversight; a second labeller is under consideration by the owner.
what_is_NOT_pinned_by_this_file: The over-refusal PAPER NUMBER, which comes from human labels (Revision 4), not from a judge.
